# third_party

Third-party files that the code reads from the repository tree: the antiword program that converts `.doc` files to text,
its character tables and Debian package, and the fastText model that identifies the language of a text.

The repository root is described in the [root README](../README.md). None of these files is generated by the code.
Their licences, copyright holders and sources are in the [Licences](#licences) section at the end of this file.

## Files

| File | Content | Read by |
|---|---|---|
| `antiword/antiword_0.37-16_amd64.deb` | Debian package of antiword 0.37 for x86-64 | `start.sh` (app startup), only when `antiword` is not on the `PATH` yet |
| `antiword/bin/antiword` | antiword executable, x86-64 ELF | Parsing pipeline, task `3_parse` (`utils/parsing_pipeline/format_parsers.py`) |
| `antiword/share/` | Character tables (`UTF-8.txt`, `cp*.txt`, `8859-*.txt`, `MacRoman.txt`, `koi8-*.txt`, `roman.txt`) and `fontnames` | Parsing pipeline, through the `ANTIWORDHOME` variable of the antiword call |
| `fasttext/lid.176.ftz` | fastText language-identification model (176 languages) | `server/services/chat/config.py` (`FASTTEXT_MODEL_PATH`), used by `translation_bridge.py` |

## Who reads each file

- **The app** calls `antiword` by its name on the `PATH` (`server/services/compare/conversion.py`), with `-m UTF-8.txt` so that accents come out in UTF-8; the table is found in `$HOME/.antiword`. `start.sh` installs
  the program into `$HOME/.local/bin` and copies the tables of the `.deb` into `$HOME/.antiword` (the `ANTIWORD_DATA`
  variable). It never reads `third_party/antiword/bin/` or `third_party/antiword/share/`.
- **The parsing pipeline** sets `ANTIWORD_BIN` and `ANTIWORD_SHARE_DIR` from `utils/parsing_pipeline/config.py`
  (`../../third_party/antiword/bin/antiword` and `../../third_party/antiword/share`, relative to the notebook's folder). The
  conversion runs `antiword -m UTF-8.txt -w 0 <file>` with `ANTIWORDHOME` set to the `share/` folder, and makes the
  binary executable when it is not. See [`utils/parsing_pipeline/README.md`](../utils/parsing_pipeline/README.md).
- **The fastText model** is loaded on the first language guess (`lru_cache` on `_fasttext_model()`) through the
  `fasttext` package of `requirements.txt`. The guesses come from the chat engine (`engine/queries.py`, when
  `CHAT_TRANSLATE_ONLY` is on), from the MLflow trace tag (`server/services/chat/mlflow_turns.py`) and from the
  translation bridge (`server/routers/chat/ws.py`, when `CHAT_TRANSLATE_BRIDGE_ENABLED` is `true`).

## Rules

- The `.deb` and the `bin/antiword` executable are in the repository as binaries: `.gitattributes` marks them `binary`,
  so Git never converts their line endings.
- When `start.sh` finds no `.deb` in `third_party/antiword/`, it tries `apt-get download antiword`, then the Ubuntu and Debian
  package URLs written in `start.sh`.
- The `sync` section of `databricks.yml`, `.databricksignore` and `utils/deploy/deploy_qualibot.ps1` do not exclude
  `third_party/`: these files are uploaded with the code.
- The files are replaced by hand. The readers above expect these names and paths.

## Licences

Third-party files shipped in this repository, with their licence. What the repository files do not state is marked
"to confirm". Python and JavaScript dependencies are listed in `requirements.txt` and `client/package.json`; their
licences are those of the packages.

### antiword

| | |
|---|---|
| Used for | Converting `.doc` files to text (`third_party/antiword/`) |
| Version | 0.37 (the program reports 0.37, 21 Oct 2005); Debian package `antiword_0.37-16_amd64.deb` |
| Copyright | Copyright (C) 1998-2003 A.J. (Adri) van Os, `antiword@winfield.demon.nl` |
| Source | http://www.winfield.demon.nl/index.html (as written in the Debian package's `copyright` file) |
| Licence | GNU General Public License. The Debian `copyright` file says "GNU General Public License (GPL)" without a version number; GPL-2.0 is the version to confirm |
| Files | `third_party/antiword/antiword_0.37-16_amd64.deb`, `third_party/antiword/bin/antiword`, `third_party/antiword/share/` (character tables and `fontnames` from the same package) |

antiword is run as a separate program (a subprocess), never linked into the application. The licence text and the source
of the package are available from the Debian archive (package `antiword`, version 0.37-16); to confirm the exact source
URL the team wants to cite.
